qs.q: A patient experiences a fracture following minimal trauma, and imaging reveals the break occurred through an underlying bone tumour. What term describes this type of fracture?
qs.e: A pathological fracture is defined as a fracture that occurs through bone weakened by an underlying disease process such as a tumour. A stress fracture results from repeated mechanical overload rather than structural weakening by disease.
qs.s: Bone & Soft Tissue Pathology: Cases, Tumors, & Answers: MCQs

qs.q: A 16-year-old male presents with a bone tumour measuring 2.5 cm located in the posterior elements of his lumbar spine. He complains of dull back pain that does not respond dramatically to aspirin. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
qs.e: Osteoblastomas are larger than 2 cm and typically occur in the posterior elements of the spine without showing a dramatic pain response to aspirin. An osteoid osteoma is smaller than 2 cm and classically features severe night pain relieved by aspirin.
